transcript:
Header:
Date: 2027-09-03
Time: 16:00 PT
Duration: ~55 minutes
Attendees: Maya (CEO), Jonas (CTO), Alex (VP Eng), Samir (Head Product), Lena (Head People), Ivy (Head CSM) + all company dial-in

Summary (auto): Maya opens with wins and risk signals; Jonas covers infra and Dedicated/Private milestones; Alex explains engineering re-org and capacity tests; Samir walks roadmap; Lena addresses compensation and hiring posture; open Q&A covers remote policy, incident handling, and DEI hiring goals.

Topics: Hiring, Performance, Product Rollouts, People/Comp, Ops

Transcript Body:
00:00 Maya: ok hey everyone good afternoon, thanks for joining, I know some of you are in EU so — appreciate the time. Quick knee on the wins, then we have focused updates from Jonas and Samir and then Q&A.
00:18 Maya: first, quick highlight — traffic growth across hosted api was up ~38% month on month, that's across several accounts, latency SLOs held during the spike, shout out to infra.
00:30 Jonas: yeah great work, team. We saw a handful of tail regressions during the big ingest window last week, root cause was a mem fragmentation pattern in the kv cache path, patched on canary, fix rolled to main. There may still be a small regression at very long sequences, we're tracking it.
00:48 Alex: and to add to that, we're starting a bench run this coming week to validate cross-region caching, because some customers run multi-region and that's where we saw most of the edge cases.
01:07 Samir: product wise, our bet for Q4 is twofold: 1) finalize Dedicated autoscaling with burst policies, 2) ship Private 1.2 with simplified KMS integration and improved audit log surface. Those are the things we think will move enterprise adoption.
01:34 Ivy: on the customer side, we've got three pilot commitments for Dedicated in the pipeline and two security reviews lined up for Private. Those could convert to multi-quarter contracts.
01:48 Lena: important people note — hiring cadence will slow for non-critical IC roles starting next pay cycle; we're prioritizing key hires in infra, se, and go-to-market. We'll still backfill critical churn and growth roles.
02:07 Maya: I want to call out stewardship — not just headcount but how we protect culture when we scale. Lena and I will lead a stewardship working group to update manager training and interview calibration.
02:25 Jonas: small re-org in infra: we are collapsing the runtime optimizations team into the serving runtime squad to speed up kernel-to-deploy cycles. This reduces handoffs. No involuntary moves, mostly remapping leads.
02:45 Alex: yep and part of that is shifting a couple of senior engs into an on-call reliability pool for Dedicated capacity nights. We'll publish the schedule and runbook.
03:05 Audience: um quick q — what does slowing hiring mean for IC promotion ladders?
03:11 Lena: good question, promotions will still continue on cycle, compensation calibrations are moving forward, we will prioritize merit and impact. We will share the calibration timeline and a Q&A doc.
03:28 Audience: second q — remote-first policy changes?
03:33 Maya: short answer no, we remain remote-first. We will tighten some expectations around overlap hours for specific cross-functional roles, and managers will be asked to ensure key meetings are accessible asynchronous.
03:51 Samir: roadmap detail — on Optimize, we're intensifying efforts on batching heuristics and quant recommendations, this will cut per-token costs for ML-heavy customers. Also, we plan to surface a cost-estimator in console by early Q4.
04:15 Jonas: dedicated milestone: we're moving to a phased SLA model — baseline SLA for reserved pools, premium SLA for guaranteed tails. We'll be clear about latency bands and billing.
04:34 Alex: technical note — the Dedicated benchmark doc will include p99 and p999 numbers for common seq lengths and for mixed workloads. It'll also include guidance for recommended quant profiles.
04:50 Ivy: sales ops and solutions engineering to run a two-week canary with two reference customers after the v1 release, this helps validate our autoscaler.
05:02 Maya: on risk signals — we still have some capacity constraints in a couple of regions; procurement lead times for certain gpu types remain long. We're making bets on alternate instance types and deeper caching to mitigate.
05:21 Jonas: also want to flag third-party dependency risk — some kernel patches are dependent on vendor driver fixes; we have a mitigation plan but it's not zero risk.
05:36 Audience (various): can we get more transparency into cost buckets in invoices?
05:42 Ivy: yes, cx teams are working with finance to add token-level cost breakdowns for enterprise invoices and a self-serve CSV export.
05:55 Audience: what about security audits — SOC2 still in flight?
06:00 Jonas: SOC2 type II is scheduled for end of Q4, we're prepping audit artifacts now; Private customers will see additional attestations and a stronger audit log feed.
06:18 Lena: quick people update — new hire orientation will be reworked into a 2-week onboarding lab where new engineers pair with incumbent owners on production tasks. We're piloting it next month.
06:36 Maya: open floor Q&A — I want to take two live questions and then we'll wrap.
06:41 Audience: question — with the slower hiring posture, will there be adjustments to bonuses?
06:47 Lena: bonuses are on the same cadence, we are not changing the bonus schedule. Calibration may affect amounts but not timing; again we'll send a FAQ.
07:02 Audience: another question — how do we ensure Dedicated doesn't cannibalize Hosted revenue?
07:09 Samir: good point. our pricing strategy is tiered; Hosted is fast on-ramp and good for variable workloads, Dedicated is for predictable throughput and enterprise SLOs. We'll aim to upsell but avoid undercutting Hosted unit economics.
07:30 Jonas: operationally we may route low-cost traffic to older quant profiles to keep unit cost down while preserving higher-quality models for premium routes.
07:44 Maya: wrap up — main asks: leadership teams publish charters, People sends comp timeline, Eng runs stress tests and posts results, Product finalizes roadmap. We will reconvene for a mid-Q check in.
08:05 Maya: thanks everyone, small housekeeping: town hall recording will be posted, comments welcome on the doc.

(There is some overlap, low audio dropouts during the open Q&A; transcription may have substituted 'kv cache' with 'k v cash' in a couple places.)
